39|BACKGROUND
40|Androgen-deprivation therapy (ADT) has been the backbone of treatment for
41|metastatic prostate cancer since the 1940s. We assessed whether concomitant
42|treatment with ADT plus docetaxel would result in longer overall survival than that
43|with ADT alone.
44|METHODS
45|We assigned men with metastatic, hormone-sensitive prostate cancer to receive
46|either ADT plus docetaxel (at a dose of 75 mg per square meter of body-surface
47|area every 3 weeks for six cycles) or ADT alone. The primary objective was to test
48|the hypothesis that the median overall survival would be 33.3% longer among
49|patients receiving docetaxel added to ADT early during therapy than among pa-
50|tients receiving ADT alone.
51|RESULTS
52|A total of 790 patients (median age, 63 years) underwent randomization. After a
53|median follow-up of 28.9 months, the median overall survival was 13.6 months
54|longer with ADT plus docetaxel (combination therapy) than with ADT alone (57.6
55|months vs. 44.0 months; hazard ratio for death in the combination group, 0.61;
56|95% confidence interval [CI], 0.47 to 0.80; P<0.001). The median time to bio-
57|chemical, symptomatic, or radiographic progression was 20.2 months in the com-
58|bination group, as compared with 11.7 months in the ADT-alone group (hazard
59|ratio, 0.61; 95% CI, 0.51 to 0.72; P<0.001). The rate of a prostate-specific antigen
60|level of less than 0.2 ng per milliliter at 12 months was 27.7% in the combination
61|group versus 16.8% in the ADT-alone group (P<0.001). In the combination group,
62|the rate of grade 3 or 4 febrile neutropenia was 6.2%, the rate of grade 3 or 4
63|infection with neutropenia was 2.3%, and the rate of grade 3 sensory neuropathy
64|and of grade 3 motor neuropathy was 0.5%.
65|CONCLUSIONS
66|Six cycles of docetaxel at the beginning of ADT for metastatic prostate cancer re-
67|sulted in significantly longer overall survival than that with ADT alone. (Funded by
68|the National Cancer Institute and others; ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT00309985.)

5|egressions of metastatic prostate
6|cancer were first documented in the 1940s
7|and were achieved with surgical castra-
8|tion; subsequently, androgen-deprivation therapy
9|(ADT) became the mainstay of therapy.1 Attempts
10|to improve the efficacy or decrease the treatment
11|burden of ADT have included the use of anti
12|androgens alone, intermittent dosing of ADT,
13|and the use of an antiandrogen combined with
14|medical or surgical castration.2-4 A meta-analysis
15|revealed an increase in survival of 3 percentage
16|points at 5 years with concurrent use of a non-
17|steroidal antiandrogen at the time of initiation
18|of ADT.2 However, resistance to ADT occurs in
19|most patients, with the result that the median
20|survival among patients with metastatic prostate
21|cancer is approximately 3 years.5,6 In patients
22|with resistance to ADT, docetaxel therapy re-
23|sulted in a median survival that was approxi-
24|mately 2.5 months longer than that with mito-
25|xantrone and prednisone.7,8
26|Prior studies of chemotherapy plus ADT, which
27|did not show a benefit, were small studies that
28|involved primarily patients with a relatively low
29|tumor burden.9,10 Definitions of a high burden of
30|disease have included the presence of visceral
31|metastases, a bone-metastasis burden categorized
32|by site (beyond the axial skeleton) or by a high
33|number of lesions, or a combination of these.9,11,12
34|In this study, the E3805 study, patients received
35|ADT alone or ADT plus docetaxel at the begin-
36|ning of ADT for metastatic hormone-sensitive
37|prostate cancer, and stratification was performed
38|prospectively according to high or low burden of
39|metastatic disease.
40|Methods
41|Study Oversight
42|The primary objective of the E3805 study was to
43|determine whether docetaxel therapy at the be-
44|ginning of ADT for metastatic hormone-sensitive
45|prostate cancer would result in longer overall
46|survival than that with ADT alone. The study was
47|designed in 2005 by the Eastern Cooperative On-
48|cology Group (ECOG; now part of ECOG-ACRIN)
49|and was approved by the institutional review
50|board at each participating institution. The study
51|was coordinated by the ECOG-ACRIN Cancer
52|Research Group. The ECOG-ACRIN Statistical
53|Center collected the data and was the leading
54|cooperative group and data coordinating center.
55|The first two authors attest that the study was
56|conducted and monitored as specified by the
57|protocol. The first author wrote the first draft of
58|the manuscript, with subsequent contributions
59|by all the coauthors. The authors vouch for the
60|accuracy and completeness of the data presented.
61|The protocol with the statistical analysis plan
62|is available with the full text of this article at
63|NEJM.org. Sanofi donated the docetaxel for
64|early use (i.e., before progression during ADT)
65|and provided a grant to ECOG-ACRIN but had
66|no role in the design of the protocol, the collec-
67|tion or analysis of the data, or the preparation of
68|the manuscript.
69|Patients
70|Patients were enrolled by ECOG-ACRIN, the
71|Southwest Oncology Group, the Alliance for
72|Clinical Trials in Oncology, and NRG Oncology
73|(a merged group that includes the National Sur-
74|gical Adjuvant Breast and Bowel Project, the Ra-
75|diation Therapy Oncology Group, and the Gyne-
76|cologic Oncology Group) and through the Clinical
77|Trials Support Unit. Eligible patients had a
78|pathological diagnosis of prostate cancer or a
79|clinical scenario consistent with prostate cancer
80|with an elevated prostate-specific antigen (PSA)
81|level; radiologic evidence of metastatic disease;
82|and an ECOG performance-status score of 0, 1,
83|or 2 (on a scale from 0 to 5, with higher scores
84|indicating greater disability; patients with a score
85|of 2 were eligible if the decrement in function-
86|ing was due to prostate cancer). Prior adjuvant
87|ADT was allowed if the duration of therapy was
88|24 months or less and progression had occurred
89|more than 12 months after completion of ther-
90|apy. Patients who were receiving ADT for meta-
91|static disease were eligible if there was no evidence
92|of progression and treatment had commenced
93|within 120 days before randomization. Organ
94|function that was adequate for docetaxel treat-
95|ment was required (details are provided in the
96|protocol). All patients provided written informed
97|consent in accordance with institutional and
98|federal guidelines.
99|Treatment Plan, Stratification,
100|and Randomization
101|Patients were randomly assigned to ADT alone
102|or to combination therapy with ADT plus doce
103|taxel at a dose of 75 mg per square meter of
104|body-surface area given every 3 weeks for six

4|cycles, with premedication with 8 mg of oral
5|dexamethasone at 12 hours, 3 hours, and 1 hour
6|before docetaxel infusion. Daily prednisone was
7|not required. Patients were stratified according
8|to age (<70 years vs. ≥70 years), ECOG perfor-
9|mance-status score (0 or 1 vs. 2), and planned
10|use of combined androgen blockade for more
11|than 30 days (yes vs. no) or agents approved for
12|prevention of skeletal-related events in castration-
13|resistant disease (zoledronic acid or denosumab)
14|(yes vs. no). Patients were also stratified accord-
15|ing to the duration of prior adjuvant ADT (<12
16|months vs. ≥12 months) and the extent of metas-
17|tases (high volume [defined as the presence of
18|visceral metastases or ≥4 bone lesions with ≥1
19|beyond the vertebral bodies and pelvis] vs. low
20|volume). Patients were required to take at least
21|500 mg of oral calcium carbonate and at least
22|400 IU of vitamin D per day.
23|Dose Modifications
24|No dose modifications of ADT were allowed,
25|and the use of a nonsteroidal antiandrogen with
26|castration (medical or surgical) at the time of
27|initiation of therapy was at the discretion of the
28|investigator. Intermittent hormonal therapy was
29|not allowed. For docetaxel, no more than two
30|dose modifications (decreases to 65 mg per
31|square meter and 55 mg per square meter) were
32|allowed. Dose adjustments were made according
33|to the organ system that showed the greatest de-
34|gree of toxic effects, which were graded accord-
35|ing to the National Cancer Institute (NCI) Com-
36|mon Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events
37|(CTCAE; version 3.0 until September 2011 and
38|version 4.0 thereafter). Details on dosing are
39|provided in the protocol. If a dose was reduced
40|owing to toxic effects, it was not increased sub-
41|sequently, and docetaxel was discontinued if
42|administration was delayed longer than 3 weeks
43|from the scheduled day of dosing. The use of
44|growth factors was at the discretion of the inves-
45|tigator.
46|Monitoring of Toxic Effects and Efficacy
47|Patients assigned to combination therapy were
48|seen every 3 weeks during the period of docetaxel
49|administration and then every 3 months. Patients
50|assigned to ADT alone were seen every 3 months.
51|For the reporting of serious adverse events to the
52|NCI and to guide dose modifications, CTCAE
53|version 3.0 was used until September 2011, at
54|which time the study began using version 4.0. To
55|ensure consistency, case-report forms for toxic
56|effects that were recorded in the study database
57|retained the use of version 3.0. All grade 3 or
58|higher toxic effects in the combination group
59|were captured, and an attribution of relatedness
60|to study therapy was made by the local investiga-
61|tors. Adverse events among patients assigned to
62|ADT alone were not routinely documented, al-
63|though major adverse events were to be reported.
64|PSA levels were measured at each scheduled
65|visit. Imaging (computed tomography [CT] of
66|the abdomen and pelvis, technetium-99m bone
67|scanning, and radiography or CT of the chest)
68|was performed at baseline and at the time of
69|documented castration resistance or as clinically
70|indicated. Disease progression on imaging was
71|determined according to the Response Evaluation
72|Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST), version 1.013
73|(the criteria are summarized in the protocol). A
74|complete serologic response was defined as a
75|PSA level of less than 0.2 ng per milliliter on two
76|consecutive measurements at least 4 weeks apart.
77|Serologic progression was defined as an increase
78|in the PSA level of more than 50% above the
79|nadir reached after the initiation of ADT, with
80|two consecutive increases at least 2 weeks apart.
81|The date of a first recorded increase of more
82|than 50% above the nadir was deemed the date
83|of progression. If the nadir level was less than
84|2 ng per milliliter, a minimum increase of more
85|than 2 ng per milliliter was required.
86|All time-to-event end points were determined
87|from the time of randomization. Overall survival
88|was defined as the time until death from any
89|cause. The time to castration-resistant prostate
90|cancer was defined as the time until document-
91|ed clinical or serologic progression with a testos-
92|terone level of less than 50 ng per deciliter (or
93|source documentation of medical castration or
94|surgical castration). The time to clinical pro-
95|gression was defined as the time until increas-
96|ing symptoms of bone metastases; progression
97|according to RECIST, version 1.0; or clinical
98|deterioration due to cancer according to the in-
99|vestigator's opinion.
100|Statistical Analysis
101|The study underwent two major amendments
102|(details are provided in the protocol); in all ver-
103|sions, an intention-to-treat analysis plan was
104|used. With each amendment, the sample size

4|was adjusted so that the study would have 80%
5|power to detect a 33.3% difference in median
6|overall survival between the combination group
7|and the ADT-alone group, with the use of a
8|stratified log-rank test at a one-sided alpha level
9|of 2.5%. At study inception, only patients with
10|high-volume disease were to be enrolled, and the
11|sample size was to be 568 patients. After com-
12|pletion of enrollment in the NCI-sponsored
13|S9346 trial,4 an amendment to the E3805 study
14|was made in July 2008, after 53 patients had been
15|enrolled, to include patients with low-volume
16|disease. A prospective stratification of high vol-
17|ume versus low volume of metastatic disease
18|was added, and the sample size was increased to
19|600 patients. The final amendment was made in
20|December 2011, after 579 patients had been en-
21|rolled, to reflect new data documenting an in-
22|crease in median overall survival owing to the
23|use of PSA in the detection and monitoring of
24|disease activity5 (initial projections were based
25|on studies from the pre-PSA era) and to address
26|the September 2011 report of the data and safety
27|monitoring committee, which noted that 70% of
28|enrolled patients had high-volume disease. The
29|final design required the enrollment of 780 pa-
30|tients, with projections of median overall sur-
31|vival with ADT alone of 33 months among pa-
32|tients with high-volume disease and 67 months
33|among patients with low-volume disease.
34|Interim analyses were to be performed before
35|all semiannual meetings of the data and safety
36|monitoring committee starting when approxi-
37|mately 25% of the planned full information was
38|obtained and continuing until either the criteria
39|for early stopping were met or full information
40|was obtained (after 399 deaths). The study was
41|monitored for early stopping for futility with the
42|use of repeated-confidence-interval methods.14 At
43|each interim analysis, the nominal (1 - [2 × alpha])
44|confidence interval for the hazard ratio for death
45|in the comparison of the combination-therapy
46|group with the ADT-alone group was computed.
47|For a given analysis time (information fraction),
48|alpha was set at the nominal one-sided signifi-
49|cance level of the use function boundary. Infor-
50|mation from interim analyses was reviewed by
51|members of the independent data and safety
52|monitoring committee, who determined wheth-
53|er efficacy or futility had been demonstrated and
54|who decided whether the study should be stopped
55|and the results reported early.
56|Descriptive statistics were used to characterize
57|patients at study entry. Kaplan-Meier estimates15
58|were used for event-time distributions. Cox pro-
59|portional-hazard models,16 stratified according
60|to the factors described above, were used to esti-
61|mate hazard ratios for time-to-event end points.
62|Stratified log-rank tests17 were used to compare
63|event-time distributions between the two groups.
64|Response rates were compared with the use of
65|Fisher's exact test.18 An intention-to-treat analy-
66|sis was conducted that included all randomly
67|assigned patients regardless of eligibility and
68|treatment status. P values are two-sided, and con-
69|fidence intervals are at the 95% level.
70|Results
71|Patients
72|From July 2006 through December 2012, a total
73|of 790 patients were enrolled and underwent ran-
74|domization. Ten patients were ineligible, 7 had
75|incomplete information to assess eligibility, and
76|6 patients in the combination group did not
77|start the assigned therapy (Fig. S1 in the Supple-
78|mentary Appendix, available at NEJM.org). All
79|randomly assigned patients were followed and
80|included in the primary analysis of their assigned
81|group. At the planned interim analysis in Octo-
82|ber 2013, a total of 53% of the planned full in-
83|formation had been obtained, prespecified crite-
84|ria for significance had been met, and the data
85|were released by the data and safety monitoring
86|committee. This report represents data with a
87|cutoff date for survival of December 23, 2013;
88|the median follow-up was 28.9 months, with
89|136 deaths in the ADT-alone group and 101
90|deaths in the combination group. All other data
91|reflect the database as of December 23, 2014.
92|Patient characteristics were well balanced be-
93|tween the two groups (Table 1). The median age
94|was 64 years (range, 36 to 88) in the combina-
95|tion group and 63 years (range, 39 to 91) in the
96|ADT-alone group. In both groups, approximately
97|85% of the patients were white, approximately
98|70% had an ECOG performance-status score of 0,

100|approximately 60% had a Gleason score of 8 or
101|higher (on a scale from 2 to 10, with higher
102|scores indicating a more aggressive form of pros-
103|tate cancer and a worse prognosis). In both
104|groups, 73% of the patients had received no

4|docetaxel given at the time ADT was initiated for
5|hormone-sensitive disease resulted in better can-
6|cer control than that with ADT alone, with a
7|longer time to the development of castration resis-
8|tance, a higher rate of decrease of the PSA level
9|to less than 0.2 ng per milliliter at 12 months, a
10|lower number of prostate-cancer deaths, and
11|substantially longer overall survival. The longer
12|overall survival than that with ADT alone was
13|achieved despite the fact that almost half the 287
14|patients who received ADT alone and then met
15|the criteria for castration resistance received
16|docetaxel at the time of disease progression
17|along with other therapies that prolong overall
18|survival in patients with metastatic castration-
19|resistant prostate cancer.
20|The definition of high-volume disease used
21|for this protocol was a combination of features
22|from prior classifications. All the definitions
23|included the presence of nonnodal, soft-tissue
24|visceral disease as a predictor of poor prognosis.
25|This protocol made use of sites of bone metas-
26|tases and the number of metastases to avoid
27|classifying patients with three or fewer sites as
28|having high-volume disease even if one lesion
29|was beyond the vertebrae and pelvis (any lesion
30|beyond the vertebrae and pelvis, irrespective of
31|total lesion count, would be classified as "exten-
32|sive" according to the definition of the South-
33|west Oncology Group4). In the subgroup of pa-
34|tients with high-volume disease, the median
35|overall survival was 17.0 months longer in the
36|combination group than in the ADT-alone group
37|(49.2 months vs. 32.2 months). On the basis of

41|disease (according to the definition used in our
42|protocol) in the ADT-alone group, and as such,
43|the definition was reproducible across two phase
